briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Trial Dates & Tailwinds: Michigan's Tax Fight Heats Up as National Cannabis and Psychedelics Momentum Builds
briefs.top: Michigan operators finally get their day in court this month as the industry's lawsuit over the 24% wholesale tax heads to trial, while the GOP's gubernatorial nominee makes repeal a campaign centerpiece. Nationally, the DEA's Schedule III hearing has reached closing arguments and Compass Pathways is racing toward a landmark psilocybin approval — real signs the regulatory tide is turning in the industry's favor.

local.text: The Michigan Cannabis Industry Association's original lawsuit challenging the 24% wholesale tax is finally heading to trial this month, giving operators their most concrete shot yet at overturning the levy in court.

Republican gubernatorial nominee John James has pledged to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax if elected in November, arguing it drives up prices and hands illicit operators a competitive edge — a real path to relief on the ballot.
Fields Cannary's hospitality-driven dispensary-restaurant buildout in Muskegon is still moving forward, proof that ambitious cannabis retail concepts are pushing ahead even under tax pressure.

JARS Cannabis reached an agreement with Madison Heights to remove a Flock surveillance camera that had been trained on its parking lot, closing out a years-long dispute stemming from the chain's original licensing fight.

The 24% wholesale tax generated roughly $37 million in Q2 and $34 million in Q1 — a fraction of the $105 million per quarter state officials projected — fueling the bipartisan repeal push and MiCIA's legal challenge.

national.text: The federal marijuana rescheduling case reached its closing-argument stage in late August, moving the DEA's Schedule III hearing closer to a final recommendation after years of delay.

Compass Pathways is ramping up commercial-readiness efforts — including a new U.S. doctor education campaign debuting at Psych Congress this month — as it targets a Q4 2026 NDA submission and a possible first-half-2027 launch for its psilocybin depression treatment.

The FDA's newly finalized psychedelic clinical trial guidance, paired with a September 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelic use, is being read by Jefferies analysts as signaling "a more supportive regulatory environment" for Compass Pathways, Atai Life Sciences, Cybin and GH Research.

Vireo Growth is on track to become the largest U.S. cannabis operator by dispensary count — roughly 270 stores — after closing the Hawthorne, Eaze and Bridgewell deals and announcing acquisitions of FLUENT and C21 to expand its Florida and Nevada footprint.

The federal ban on hemp THC products, originally set for November 12, has been pushed back to December 11 under a bill President Trump signed, buying the industry another month to shape guardrails instead of an outright ban.
